# ADIF Lint rules

<!-- Generated by tests/conformance_tests from src/core/adif_rules.cpp and tests/conformance/rules.cases. Do not edit:
     build/conformance_tests tests/conformance/rules.cases --write-doc docs/RULES.md -->

Every finding ADIF Lint reports names one of these rules by its code, as the command line prints it (`[length]`) and Check Log groups it. Each rule says where in the ADIF specification it comes from (section numbers are ADIF 3.1.8's), which file formats it applies to, and what a conforming file does. [ADIF conformance](ADIF_CONFORMANCE.md) says how the rules were drawn up and verified.

The conformance tests (`tests/conformance/rules.cases`) hold, for every rule and each format it applies to, at least one case that breaks the rule and one that keeps it; each case is written once and built as an ADI file, an ADX file or both, and checked against any ADIF version. The example column shows a case that breaks the rule, in the cases' notation: fields with their lengths left out, a record's QSO_DATE, TIME_ON, CALL, BAND and MODE filled in (`bare`: not), `||` after header fields, `|` between records, and `raw:` before a whole file.

97 rules, 233 cases.

## ADI structure

| Code | Section | Formats | Severity | A conforming file | Breaks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tag-syntax` | IV.A.1 | ADI | error, warning | A data specifier is &lt;F:L&gt; or &lt;F:L:T&gt;: a field name, a colon, an unsigned decimal length, and optionally a colon and a one-letter type indicator, in angle brackets. *An error when the text was meant as a specifier (it has a colon or names a field), else a warning for a stray '&lt;'.* | `raw:log\n<EOH>\n<QSO_DATE:8>20240115 <CALL:4W1AW <EOR>\n` |
| `length` | IV.A.1 | ADI | error | L is the length of the data D that follows the specifier: importers read exactly L bytes (or characters, a setting). *Also reported when the data ends with a line break that L counts. Fix Lengths repairs it.* | `raw:log\n<EOH>\n<QSO_DATE:8>20240115 <CALL:3>W1AW<BAND:3>20m<EOR>\n` |
| `length-zeros` | IV.A.1, Resources III.B | ADI | warning | A data length has no leading zeros: they are import-only. *Fix Lengths removes them.* | `raw:log\n<EOH>\n<QSO_DATE:8>20240115 <CALL:04>W1AW <EOR>\n` |
| `length-swallows` | IV.A.1 | ADI | warning | The data holds no well-formed data specifier: if it does, a length that is too long has swallowed the next field. *A heuristic.* | `raw:log\n<EOH>\n<QSO_DATE:8>20240115 <NAME:16>Bob <BAND:3>20m <EOR>\n` |
| `missing-lt` | IV.A.6 | ADI | warning | Text outside data specifiers is ignored, so what looks like a specifier missing its '&lt;' (CALL:4&gt;W1AW) is lost with its data. | `raw:log\n<EOH>\n<CALL:4>W1AW <EOR>\nBAND:3>20m\n<CALL:4>K1AB <EOR>\n` |
| `bom` | III.A, IV.A | ADI | warning | An ADI file is ASCII, so it has no UTF-8 byte order mark. *Some importers reject the mark; the repair removes it.* | `raw:\xEF\xBB\xBFlog\n<EOH>\n<CALL:4>W1AW <EOR>\n` |
| `eoh-missing` | IV.A.3 | ADI | error, warning, note | A file that does not start with '&lt;' starts with a header, which &lt;EOH&gt; ends. *An error when the file holds only header fields, a warning when text begins a header that records follow, a note when only white space comes before the first '&lt;'.* | `raw:log\n<ADIF_VER:5>3.1.8\n` |
| `eoh-no-header` | IV.A.3 | ADI | warning | A file that starts with '&lt;' has no header, so it has no &lt;EOH&gt;. | `raw:<ADIF_VER:5>3.1.8 <EOH>\n<CALL:4>W1AW <EOR>\n` |
| `eoh-twice` | IV.A.2 | ADI | error | A file has at most one header, so one &lt;EOH&gt;. | `raw:log\n<EOH>\n<EOH>\n<CALL:4>W1AW <EOR>\n` |
| `eoh-late` | IV.A.2 | ADI | error | The header comes before the records. | `raw:<CALL:4>W1AW <EOR>\n<EOH>\n` |
| `no-eor` | IV.A.6 | ADI | error | Every record ends with &lt;EOR&gt;. *The repair adds it.* | `raw:log\n<EOH>\n<CALL:4>W1AW\n` |
| `empty-record` | IV.A.6 | ADI, ADX | warning | A record is one or more fields, then &lt;EOR&gt; (in ADX, a RECORD element). *The ADX schemas allow an empty RECORD, which carries no QSO all the same.* | `bare` |
| `no-records` | IV.A.2 | ADI | note | An ADI file has one or more records. *A note: Start Activation and the QSO panel create a log before its first QSO. ADX allows zero records (IV.B).* | `raw:log\n<ADIF_VER:5>3.1.8\n<EOH>\n` |

## ADX structure

| Code | Section | Formats | Severity | A conforming file | Breaks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `xml` | IV.B; XML 1.0 | ADX | error, warning | An ADX file is well-formed XML. *Only the first error is reported: what follows mostly follows from it, and nothing else is checked.* | `raw:<?xml version="1.0"?>\n<ADX><HEADER/><RECORDS><RECORD><CALL>W1AW</RECORD></RECORDS></ADX>\n` |
| `adx-encoding` | IV.B | ADX | error | An ADX file is UTF-8; an XML declaration names no other encoding. | `raw:<?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO-8859-1"?>\n<ADX><HEADER><ADIF_VER>3.1.8</ADIF_VER></HEADER><RECORDS/></ADX>\n` |
| `adx-doctype` | IV.B.1 | ADX | error | An ADX file has no document type declaration (&lt;!DOCTYPE ...&gt;). | `raw:<?xml version="1.0"?>\n<!DOCTYPE ADX>\n<ADX><HEADER><ADIF_VER>3.1.8</ADIF_VER></HEADER><RECORDS/></ADX>\n` |
| `adx-entity` | IV.B.1 | ADX | error | An ADX file uses no entities but those XML predefines (&amp;amp; &amp;lt; &amp;gt; &amp;apos; &amp;quot;). *Character references (&amp;#233;) are not entities and are fine. An entity that is not declared at all is an xml error.* | `raw:<?xml version="1.0"?>\n<!DOCTYPE ADX [<!ENTITY tb "160m">]>\n<ADX><HEADER><ADIF_VER>3.1.8</ADIF_VER></HEADER><RECORDS><RECORD><CALL>W1AW</CALL>…` |
| `adx-cdata` | IV.B.1 | ADX | error | A field's element holds no CDATA section. *CDATA between fields, in a RECORD's mixed content, is allowed. XML namespaces and processing instructions are ignored, as IV.B.1 says.* | `raw:<?xml version="1.0"?>\n<ADX><HEADER><ADIF_VER>3.1.8</ADIF_VER></HEADER><RECORDS><RECORD><CALL>W1AW</CALL><COMMENT><![CDATA[a < b]]></COMMENT></…` |

## Header

| Code | Section | Formats | Severity | A conforming file | Breaks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `adif-ver` | III.C.1.a | ADI, ADX | warning | ADIF_VER is X.Y.Z, X an integer and Y and Z digits. | `<ADIF_VER>3.1 \|\| <CALL>W1AW` |
| `created-timestamp` | III.C.1.a | ADI, ADX | error | CREATED_TIMESTAMP is 'YYYYMMDD HHMMSS': a Date, a space and a 6-digit Time, UTC. | `<ADIF_VER>3.1.8 <CREATED_TIMESTAMP>20240115 250000 \|\| <CALL>W1AW` |

## Fields

| Code | Section | Formats | Severity | A conforming file | Breaks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `unknown-field` | III.C, IV.A.4, IV.A.5, IV.B.2, IV.B.3 | ADI, ADX | warning | A field is an ADIF field of the version checked, an application-defined field (APP_...) or a user-defined field the header defines. *In ADX, a record's USERDEF must name a field the header defines.* | `<FOO>bar` |
| `field-version` | II.A, III.C | ADI, ADX | warning | A field belongs to the ADIF version the file is checked against. *The message names the version that brought the field.* | `<POTA_REF>K-0001` |
| `field-place` | III.C.1.a, III.C.1.b, IV.A.5 | ADI, ADX | warning | Header fields (and USERDEFn) are in the header, QSO fields in records. | `<PROGRAMID>MonoLog` |
| `dup-field` | III.C.1.a, III.C.1.b | ADI, ADX | error | No field name appears twice in the header, nor twice in one record. *A repair is offered when both copies agree or one is empty.* | `<NAME>Bob <NAME>Robert` |
| `import-only` | II.B | ADI, ADX | warning | Deprecated (import-only) fields, enumeration values and data types are read on import but not written on export. *The repair applies the replacement the specification names.* | `<VE_PROV>ON` |
| `intl-adi` | IV.A.1, III.A | ADI | error, note | Fields of the Intl types (IntlString, IntlMultilineString) are not used in ADI files. *A note for a USERDEF of an Intl type: it is fine, but can carry data only in ADX.* | `<NAME_INTL>Jos\xC3\xA9` |
| `indicator` | III.A, IV.A.1 | ADI, ADX | error, warning | A data type indicator is one of the letters III.A lists (B N D T S I M G E L), and agrees with the field's type. *An unknown letter is an error, one that contradicts the field a warning. In ADX, APP's and USERDEF's TYPE.* | `<APP_MONOLOG_SPEED:Q>18` |

## Enumerations

| Code | Section | Formats | Severity | A conforming file | Breaks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enumeration` | III.B | ADI, ADX | error | An Enumeration field's value is one of its enumeration's values (case-insensitive) in the version checked. | `<BAND>21m` |
| `advisory-list` | III.C.1.b, III.B.5, III.B.25 | ADI, ADX | note | CONTEST_ID and SUBMODE are Strings whose enumerations are advisory: other values are allowed. *A note for a value not on the list, in case it is a misspelling.* | `<CONTEST_ID>MY-OWN-CONTEST` |
| `deleted-code` | II.C | ADI, ADX | warning | A deleted enumeration value is only used for QSOs within the dates it was valid (ARRL sections, regions, Russian and Austrian districts). *The repair applies the replacement when the specification names one valid on the QSO's date.* | `<ARRL_SECT>ON` |
| `mode-is-submode` | III.B.10, III.B.25 | ADI, ADX | error, warning | MODE is a Mode value; a submode (USB, FT4) goes in SUBMODE with its MODE. *A warning for a MODE value that was a mode and is now import-only (C4FM), an error for one that never was.* | `<MODE>USB` |
| `subdivision` | III.B.12, III.B.22 | ADI, ADX | warning | STATE and CNTY (and MY_) are codes of the record's DXCC entity, for the entities ADIF lists them for. *A warning: callbooks fill these from profiles. Other entities' values are not checked.* | `<DXCC>291 <STATE>ZZ` |
| `region-dxcc` | III.B.21 | ADI, ADX | warning | REGION is a region of the record's DXCC entity. | `<DXCC>291 <REGION>SY` |
| `subdivision-alt` | III.B.23 | ADI, ADX | warning, note | CNTY_ALT's codes are from ADIF's table for the enumeration-name, for the entity it belongs to. *A note for an enumeration-name ADIF lists no codes for.* | `<CNTY_ALT>NZ_Regions:Nowhere/Town` |

| Code | Section | Formats | Severity | A conforming file | Breaks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `range` | III.C.1.b, IV.A.5, IV.B.3 | ADI, ADX | error | A value is within its field's minimum and maximum (CQZ 1-40, AGE 0-120...), and a user field's within its RANGE. | `<AGE>121` |
| `normalize` | ANT_AZ, ANT_EL | ADI, ADX | warning | ANT_AZ is 0 to 360 and ANT_EL -90 to 90: values outside are import-only. *The repair writes the normalized value (370 as 10).* | `<ANT_AZ>370` |
| `vucc-grids` | VUCC_GRIDS, III.A.1 | ADI, ADX | error, warning | VUCC_GRIDS and MY_VUCC_GRIDS hold two or four adjacent locators, all 4 or all 6 characters. *An error for a locator that is not 4 or 6 characters, a warning for the count, mixed sizes or squares that do not touch.* | `<VUCC_GRIDS>FN,FM` |
| `grid-ext-length` | GRIDSQUARE_EXT | ADI, ADX | warning | GRIDSQUARE_EXT is written 2 or 4 characters long; importers ignore the rest. *The repair keeps the first four.* | `<GRIDSQUARE>FN31pr45 <GRIDSQUARE_EXT>ab12cd` |
| `grid-ext-base` | GRIDSQUARE_EXT | ADI, ADX | warning | GRIDSQUARE_EXT holds a locator's characters 9 and on, so GRIDSQUARE holds its first 8. | `<GRIDSQUARE>FN31 <GRIDSQUARE_EXT>ab` |
| `lat-lon` | LAT, LON, MY_LAT, MY_LON | ADI, ADX | error | LAT and MY_LAT are latitudes (N or S, at most 90 degrees); LON and MY_LON longitudes (E or W, at most 180). *Read from the fields' meaning: the Location type allows any direction.* | `<LAT>W074 00.000` |
| `qsl-date` | QSLRDATE, QSLSDATE, LOTW_, EQSL_, DCL_... | ADI, ADX | warning | A QSL date is only valid with a status that allows it: received Y, I or V; sent Y, Q or I (a missing status is N). | `<QSLRDATE>20240201` |

## ADX schemas

| Code | Section | Formats | Severity | A conforming file | Breaks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | IV.B.5, V.A | ADX | error | An ADX file is valid against the XML Schemas published for its ADIF version: the generic one, and the export one except for what the specification makes import-only. *Both run, from spec/adx/. The generic schema covers every version up to its own, so it leaves out ranges and types that changed.* | `<BAND>21m` |
| `schema-export` | II.B, IV.B.5 | ADX | warning | What the version's export schema rejects and the specification makes import-only is read, not written. | `<VE_PROV>ON` |
| `schema-strict` | IV.B.3 | ADX | warning | Where the schemas are stricter than the specification, a record's USERDEF may carry TYPE (ignored) and a FIELDNAME in mixed case. *A warning, for programs that validate.* | `<ADIF_VER>3.1.8 <USERDEF1:E>SIZE,{S,M,L} \|\| <Size>M` |
| `schema-version` | V.A | ADX | note | The schemas are those of the version checked; 3.0.2 published none, so it and older use 3.0.3's. | `<NAME>Bob` |

## Versions

| Code | Section | Formats | Severity | A conforming file | Breaks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `version-mismatch` | II.A, III.C.1.a | ADI, ADX | note | The checks follow an older ADIF version than the one the file declares. *Choose the version in Settings or Check Log, or the file's own.* | `<ADIF_VER>3.1.8 \|\| <CALL>W1AW` |
| `version-missing` | III.C.1.a | ADI, ADX | note | The file's own version was asked for, but its ADIF_VER names none this build knows, so the version in use applies. | `<PROGRAMID>MonoLog \|\| <CALL>W1AW` |

## Practice

| Code | Section | Formats | Severity | A conforming file | Breaks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `minimum-fields` | I.E, Resources III.C | ADI, ADX | note | A QSO record has QSO_DATE, TIME_ON, CALL, BAND or FREQ, and MODE: ADIF's suggested minimum. | `bare <CALL>W1AW` |
| `placeholder` | III.C.1.b | ADI, ADX | warning | A field without a value is left out, rather than holding a placeholder (none, n/a, -, ?, unknown) its type does not allow. *A warning, with removal of the field as the repair.* | `<IOTA>none` |
| `case` | LoTW, POTA | ADI, ADX | note | CALL, STATION_CALLSIGN, OPERATOR, STATE and MY_STATE are written in upper case. *Beyond the specification, which makes most values case-insensitive.* | `<CALL>w1aw` |
| `band-missing` | POTA | ADI, ADX | note | A record with FREQ has BAND too: POTA reads BAND only. | `bare <QSO_DATE>20240115 <TIME_ON>1830 <CALL>WF1B <MODE>CW <FREQ>14.025` |
| `future-date` | POTA | ADI, ADX | warning | QSO_DATE is not after today (UTC). | `<QSO_DATE>20261231` |
| `sat-name` | LoTW | ADI, ADX | note | A satellite QSO (PROP_MODE SAT) names the satellite in SAT_NAME. | `<PROP_MODE>SAT <BAND>2m` |
| `sat-prop` | LoTW | ADI, ADX | warning | A record with SAT_NAME has PROP_MODE SAT. | `<SAT_NAME>AO-7 <BAND>2m` |
| `pota-station` | POTA | ADI, ADX | note | Each record of a POTA activation log has STATION_CALLSIGN or OPERATOR. | `<MY_SIG>POTA <MY_SIG_INFO>K-0001` |
| `field-day-class` | III.B.2 | ADI, ADX | error | ARRL_SECT holds a section, not a Field Day class such as 1D (which goes in CLASS). *The ARRL_SECT enumeration error, with the repair that moves the class.* | `<ARRL_SECT>1D` |

## ADIF Lint itself

| Code | Section | Formats | Severity | A conforming file | Breaks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `adx-internal` |  | ADX | error | ADIF Lint could read the XML and apply the built-in schemas. | (none: Only when libxml2 cannot: a file over 2 GB, or a schema that does not compile (adx_tests compiles each one).) |

## What ADIF Lint does not check

| Section | The specification says | Why it is not checked |
|---|---|---|
| I.E | Applications decide which fields to support; a dependent field should be exported with the field it depends on. | Only STATE, CNTY and their MY_ forms name what they depend on (DXCC, MY_DXCC); they are checked (depends). |
| II.A | Each ADIF version is upward compatible with the earlier ones. | A rule for the specification, not for a file. |
| III.A | Digit, Character and IntlCharacter data types. | No field has them and no type indicator names them. |
| III.A.1 | Locators are based on WGS-84; applications using other encodings convert them. | Not visible in a file. |
| III.B.8 | Deleted DXCC entities. | The specification marks them deleted but gives no dates (II.C needs the dates). |
| III.B.22 | CNTY values for most entities (US counties, Japanese cities...), and deleted Alaska boroughs. | Their lists are external, or have no dates; CNTY is checked for the entities ADIF lists codes for. |
| III.B.5 | Contest IDs that have ended. | Their end dates are only in their descriptions. |
| III.C.1.b | COUNTRY, MY_COUNTRY and DARC_DOK values. | The specification refers to external lists without including them. |
| III.C.2 | The PROGRAMID register. | It is voluntary. |
| IV.A.1 | Field definitions do not limit a data length. | Nothing to check. |
| IV.A.4 | Application-defined fields should include a data type indicator. | A recommendation; without one the field is a MultilineString, which is checked. |
| IV.A | ADI files have the extension .adi; applications should accept .adif. | A file name, not its content; the plugin checks both. |
| IV.B | Element and attribute names are upper case. | The schemas check it (schema); ADIF Lint adds a hint. |
| IV.B.1 | XML namespaces and processing instructions are ignored. | ADIF Lint ignores them too: namespaces are removed before validation. |
